title: Occupancy-map + hybrid resident-slab allocator for blocked KV paging
creator: Riley Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a blocked/paged KV residency layer that uses a compact occupancy bitmap and a hybrid slab allocator to reduce GPU OOMs, minimize host<->GPU transfer spikes, and preserve tail latency under continuous batching. This ticket captures implementation details, API knobs, trade-offs, rollout path, and observability we need to ship a safe default in runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New resident allocator implements occupancy bitmap with 8KB granularity and supports atomic slot leases
2) Host spill/restore path avoids synchronous page faults during generation; p95 additional token latency from spill/restore must be < 60ms under mixed load
3) Continuous-batching latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for 1k token sequences do not regress by more than 8% on representative traces
4) Eviction rate metrics (evictions/sec) are available per model and per shard in Console and correlate with host transfer bytes
5) Automated canary (10% traffic) shows no increase in error rates or OOM incidents for 72 hours
6) Rollback feature (prefer-host-variant policy) is implemented and exercised in canary plan
design_decisions: Occupancy bitmap: use a compact bitset per KV slab to track per-extent residency (default extent=8KB). Bitmap fits in L2 cache for small slabs to allow fast in-band checks during KV lookup.
Hybrid slab allocator: combine fast fixed-size slot allocation for small KV entries (<64KB) with segmented extents for large values. This reduces fragmentation compared to pure slab-only designs.

Lease tokens: each allocation issues a short-lived lease token that pins extent residency during active batch processing. Leases are renewed by runtime when request affinity continues, otherwise expire to allow eviction.

Async host spill: eviction writes extents to host-staging with async DMA and publishes a tombstone in bitmap. Restores are performed with background prefetch triggered by batch planner's hinting (see batching integration).

Backpressure layering: integrate with admission controller—when host-staging throughput exceeds threshold, admissions are slowed and the runtime prefers fallbacks (cheaper models or host-only inference) to avoid cascading OOMs.

Batch-aware prefetch hints: batch scheduler emits prefetch windows computed from token offsets and token affinity scores so restore happens ahead of KV access window without blocking critical-path token generation.
Graceful degradation: provide a runtime policy to fall back to a compact model variant (lower memory) when residency budget is exhausted rather than hard OOMs.
Telemetry-first: expose per-model, per-shard residency percent, host-spill-bytes, avg-restore-latency-ms, lease-renewals, and failed-restore counts to Console for triage.
tradeoffs: 8KB extent vs 4KB: 8KB reduces bitmap overhead and amortizes DMA payloads but increases restore bytes for sparse hotsets. Chosen 8KB as baseline and expose knob for tuning per-customer workloads.
Lease complexity: short leases reduce unnecessary pinning but add bookkeeping and slightly increase CPU overhead. We accept modest CPU overhead to prevent tail latency spikes caused by stale pins.

Async spill consistency: the design accepts eventual consistency for residency state (bitmap tombstones) to avoid synchronous stalls. This complicates correctness when multiple replicas access same KV; we document invariant and add safety checks for multi-replica scenarios.
Prefetch heuristics vs correctness: aggressive prefetch reduces restore latency but increases host bandwidth; we default conservative heuristics and instrument to iterate with real workloads.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests for bitmap operations, slot leasing, and async spill/restore in local simulator
Phase 1 (internal): feature gated runtime build deployed to internal cluster with synthetic mixes (chatty short requests, single long-sequence traces)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% traffic on lower criticality models with monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback if OOMs increase or restore latency > 120ms
Phase 3 (gradual): incrementally increase traffic and enable knob exposures in Console for Dedicated customers to tune extent size and lease timeout
Rollback: runtime flag prefer-host-variant and force-disable-resident-allocator for emergency mitigation
test_plan: Unit: bitmap correctness (set/clear/test), lease renewal/expiration semantics, multi-threaded concurrent allocation stress test
Integration: end-to-end restore path using host-staging with simulated DMA delays, verify generation continues under eviction
Perf: identify p50/p95/p99 delta for token generation across representative workloads (search, summarization, chat) with and without resident allocator
Fault injections: host-staging IO stalls, partial restore failures, lease leak simulation
Scale: run on fleet-sized simulation reproducing typical shard counts (64, 128) to validate centralized metrics aggregation
metrics_and_observability: kv.evictions.count (counter) with eviction_reason label (age, pressure, manual)
